To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of an internal electrostatic field in the NC region of the dot-matix system is responsible for the spatial separation of electrons from holes, and for the quantum-confined Stark shift of the NCs photoluminescence.

(a) PbTe quantum dots (QD's) embedded in a matrix of CdTe are stable, (b) the QD's are electrically polarized due to the asymmetric distribution of the dot-molecule interfaces, (c) the polarization field leads to a quantum confined Stark effect, (d) the QD-matrix system has a direct gap, and (e) the QD ground state is a doublet with a spin-orbit splitting of 0.2 e

PbTe NCs embedded in a CdTeX matrix exhibit an asymmetrical distribution of polar dot/matrix interfaces that results in the presence of an electric field within the NC, which leads to spatially separated electrons and holes and, therefore, a quantum-confined stark effect that influences the photoluminiscence of the NC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ab initio approach to the calculation of the electronic structure of nanocrystals.
the electronic properties of a PbTe NC embedded in a CdTeXy matrix.
the study of the electronic structure of semiconductor quantum dots (QDs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electronic properties of NCs embedded in a matrix are not only determined by the size of the NCs, but also by the nature of the matrix and the dot-matrix interface.
the electronic properties of NCs are strongly dependent on their size, shape and the nature of their surrounding matrix.
the PbTe NCs embedded in a Cd Te matrix are not good candidates for the realization of quantum dot infrared photodetectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PbTe quantum dots in CdTe matrix can be a good candidate for the application of the quantum-confined Stark effects.
the electronic properties of NCs embedded in a matrix strongly depend on the NC-matrix interface properties.
the PbTe NCs embedded in CdTe matrix are not suitable for optoelectronic applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrostatic potential inside the NC is not negligible.
the electrostatic field inside a PbTe/CdTe NC is not a perturbation, but rather a key factor that should be taken into account when studying PbTe NCs embedded in a CdTec matrix.
the electronic structure of PbTe/CdTe nanocomposites can be understood by taking the electrostatic field into account.
